W.note: The violet aura and light sweep bloom most vividly of the four on a dark ground, but the 560ms curve is symmetric so hover-out lags, letter-spacing animates layout, and the music-player framing is a loose fit for a button study.

X.note: Asymmetric enter (360ms) and leave (180ms) curves, a separate glow curve with delay, full reduced-motion fallback, a visible focus ring and a contrast readout make it the most practical, though the halo is quieter and less ethereal.

Y.note: A pale blurred halo that fades on its own curve, a single sheen pass and a small lift feel airy, and it stays cheap (transform and opacity only) with a clear focus state, reduced-motion handling and a curve plot that makes the easing legible.

Z.note: The richest curve vocabulary (drift, bloom keyframe, breathing busy state) and polished phone layout, but the hover glow is faint in the frames, the saturated violet reads as generic SaaS, and it animates box-shadow, filter and letter-spacing, which costs more to render.
